title: Evaluated compact support and its scalar-adjunction transition
statement:
Fix the global finite-field datum $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ of characteristic $p$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], a prime $\ell\ne p$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, its valuation ring $R$, a uniformizer $\varpi$, and $A_n=R/\varpi^n$ for $n\ge1$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $a:X\to s=\operatorname{Spec}k$ be separated and of finite type [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties], and fix one compactification $a=pj$. Write $F_n=Rp_{*,n}j_!$ for compact support on ordinary small pro-etale module derived categories [def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support].

For $W=X,\bar X,s$, where $j:X\to\bar X$ is the open immersion and $p:\bar X\to s$ the proper map of the compactification, use the quotient-ring sequence site $\mathcal Q_W$ of [def-coef-ringed-sequence-site], with ring sheaf $(n,U)\mapsto(A_n)_W(U)$ and quotient restrictions. Let $Q_\bullet$ be any strict complex of quotient-semilinear module systems, and let $M_n$ be its level objects in $D(X_{\mathrm{proet}},A_n)$. Write $\sigma_{m,n}:M_m\to\operatorname{Res}_{m,n}M_n$ for its derived transitions, $T_W=-\otimes^L_{(A_m)_W}(A_n)_W$, and $\alpha_{m,n}:T_XM_m\to M_n$ for their tensor--restriction adjoints [def-coef-normalized-dvr-tower]. Normalization of $Q_\bullet$ is not required. Set
$$B(Q)=\operatorname{Res}_R R\Gamma^{\operatorname{Tow}}(s,Rp_*^{\mathcal Q}j_!Q_\bullet)\in D(\operatorname{Tow}(\operatorname{Mod}(R))),$$
where proper direct image and point sections (the sections functor $\Gamma(s,-)$ at the final object of $s_{\mathrm{proet}}$ [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point]) are derived separately, and $\operatorname{Res}_R$ uses the actual constant maps $R\to A_n$; no inverse limit in $n$ occurs [lem-weil-tower-category-levelwise-abelian]. Let $c_{m,n,M_m}:T_sF_mM_m\to F_nT_XM_m$ be the canonical compact-support coefficient projection map, formed from the exact open-extension comparison and the proper-image coefficient mate [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections]. Let $\eta$ be the unit of $T_s\dashv\operatorname{Res}_{m,n}$. Put
$$d_{m,n}=\operatorname{Res}_{m,n}\bigl(F_n(\alpha_{m,n})\circ c_{m,n,M_m}\bigr)\circ\eta_{F_mM_m}.$$
There are isomorphisms in $D(R)$, natural in the strict derived input,
$$\Theta_{Q,n}:\operatorname{ev}_n B(Q)\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Res}^{A_n}_R R\Gamma(s,F_nM_n).$$
For every $m\ge n$, $\Theta_{Q,n}\circ\operatorname{ev}(t_{m,n}^{B(Q)})=R\Gamma(s,d_{m,n})\circ\Theta_{Q,m}$, with constant-$R$ restriction understood. Equivalently $d_{m,n}$ is compact support applied to $\sigma_{m,n}$ followed by the canonical coefficient-restriction comparison. These identifications respect the identity and composition of every quotient transition. If $M_n\cong\omega_n=Ra_n^!(A_n)_s$ and $\alpha_{m,n}$ is the counit-defined $u_{m,n}$ of [lem-coef-finite-dualizing], then, after the identifications $M_n\cong\omega_n$, $c_{m,n,\omega_m}$ is the finite pro-etale realization of the compact-support coefficient comparison $c_{X,A_m,A_n,\omega_m}$ specified in [lem-coef-finite-dualizing], so $d_{m,n}=\operatorname{Res}_{m,n}(F_n(u_{m,n})\circ c_{m,n,\omega_m})\circ\eta_{F_m\omega_m}$ with that comparison. All identifications depend only on $Q_\bullet$ and the fixed compactification.

proof.text:
Identify modules on each $\mathcal Q_W$ with strict quotient-semilinear systems by [def-coef-ringed-sequence-site]. Apply [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections] to the pro-etale geometric morphism induced by $p$, with coefficient rings $(A_n)_s$ and their inverse images $(A_n)_{\bar X}$. Its direct image is the actual $Rp_*^{\mathcal Q}$, and its exact open-localization operation is the actual $j_!$. The evaluation comparisons give natural isomorphisms
$$\psi_n:e_n(Rp_*^{\mathcal Q}j_!Q)\xrightarrow{\sim}Rp_{*,n}j_!M_n=F_nM_n.$$
Exact open extension evaluates termwise; proper direct image uses the cited derived comparison, not an assertion that $e_n$ preserves K-injectives. This applies to arbitrary unbounded $Q$ and does not require its scalar-extension transitions to be invertible.

proof.text:
Write $\beta_j:T_{\bar X}j_!^m\xrightarrow{\sim}j_!^nT_X$ for the exact open scalar comparison and $b_p:T_sRp_{*,m}\to Rp_{*,n}T_{\bar X}$ for the proper coefficient mate. The open comparison is the scalar/open adjunction comparison of [lem-fix-open-scalar-tensor-normalization]; the proper comparison is the one specified in [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections]. Thus the map called $c$ in the statement is
$$c_{m,n,M}=Rp_{*,n}(\beta_{j,M})\circ b_{p,j_!M}.$$
The transition formula for proper direct image in that node, applied after exact open extension, says that under $\psi_m,\psi_n$ the extension-form transition is
$$T_sF_mM_m\xrightarrow{c_{m,n,M_m}}F_nT_XM_m\xrightarrow{F_n(\alpha_{m,n})}F_nM_n.$$
Indeed the open transition is $j_!^n(\alpha_{m,n})\beta_j$: since $\beta_j$ is the comparison of left adjoints with the common right adjoint $j^{-1}\operatorname{Res}=\operatorname{Res}j^{-1}$, the transpose of $j_!^n(\alpha_{m,n})\beta_j$ under $S_{\bar X}j_!^m\dashv j^{-1}\operatorname{Res}$ equals that of $j_!^n(\alpha_{m,n})$ under $j_!^nS_X\dashv\operatorname{Res}j^{-1}$, namely $\operatorname{Res}(\alpha_{m,n})\eta=\sigma_{m,n}$; so its scalar transpose is $j_!(\sigma_{m,n})$ under $j_!\operatorname{Res}=\operatorname{Res}j_!$, the actual termwise restriction-form transition of $j_!Q$. Substituting it in $G_n(t)\,b_p$ gives precisely the displayed word.

proof.text:
By the scalar adjunction [lem-pur-sheaf-ring-derived-coefficient-adjunction], the restriction-form arrow corresponding to any $v:T_sP\to N$ is $\operatorname{Res}(v)\eta_P$. Applying this formula to the extension-form transition in step 2 gives
$$\psi_n\,e(t_{m,n}^{Rp_*^{\mathcal Q}j_!Q})=d_{m,n}\,\psi_m,$$
where $d_{m,n}=\operatorname{Res}(F_n(\alpha_{m,n})c_{m,n,M_m})\eta_{F_mM_m}$. All these maps are in ordinary $A_m$-module derived categories, so they also give arrows after exact constant-$R$ restriction. The scalar adjunction has no flatness or boundedness hypothesis.

proof.text:
For the alternative description let $\rho:F_m\operatorname{Res}_X\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Res}_sF_n$ be [lem-sf-compact-support-restriction-of-scalars]. The proper/open scalar mate defining $c$ is also the comparison of [def-coef-compact-support-tensor-comparison]: paste the proper counit mate and the open adjunction comparison using [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting]. Its defining scalar transpose is therefore
$$\operatorname{Res}(c_M)\eta_{F_mM}=\rho_{T_XM}F_m(\eta_M).$$
Consequently naturality of $\rho$ at $\alpha:T_XM_m\to M_n$ yields
$$d_{m,n}=\operatorname{Res}(F_n\alpha)\rho_{T_XM_m}F_m\eta_{M_m}=\rho_{M_n}F_m(\operatorname{Res}(\alpha)\eta_{M_m})=\rho_{M_n}F_m(\sigma_{m,n}).$$
This proves the claimed equivalence for the specified comparisons, rather than just identifying their objects.

proof.text:
Let $g:\operatorname{Sh}(s_{\mathrm{proet}})\to\operatorname{Set}$ be global sections, with inverse image the constant-sheaf functor, and put the inverse system of rings $A_n$ on the punctual topos. Its inverse images are precisely $(A_n)_s$. Apply [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections] to $g$ and these ring systems. The resulting $Rg_{*,\bullet}$ is $R\Gamma^{\operatorname{Tow}}(s,-)$: its target is the ordinary derived category of quotient-semilinear $A_n$-module systems on the point, and it takes no inverse limit. Its evaluation comparison identifies level $n$ with $R\Gamma(s,-)$ in $A_n$-modules and carries restriction-form transitions to their derived-sections maps. Restriction along the actual maps $R\to A_n$ changes only the module action [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars]; it is exact because kernels and cokernels have unchanged underlying abelian sheaves. Evaluation commutes with it termwise. Compose this comparison with $\operatorname{Res}^{A_n}_R R\Gamma(s,\psi_n)$ to define $\Theta_{Q,n}$. Step 3 and naturality now give the required equation
$$\Theta_{Q,n}\,e(t_{m,n}^{B(Q)})=R\Gamma(s,d_{m,n})\,\Theta_{Q,m}$$
in $D(R)$. Both derivations have been performed separately, as required.

proof.text: The comparisons used in steps 1 and 5 are natural on ordinary derived categories and compatible with all transition maps by [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections]. In the actual strict tower underlying $B(Q)$ one has $t_{n,n}=1$ and $t_{r,n}=t_{m,n}t_{r,m}$. Conjugating these equations by the isomorphisms $\Theta$ proves their counterparts on the evaluated section objects. The same statement before sections, using $\psi$ and scalar restriction, proves identity and composition for $d$. No conclusion is deduced from evaluations detecting equality of arbitrary morphisms. All comparison maps were specified by the actual functors for $j,p,g$ and their derived natural comparisons; hence they are natural in derived $Q$ and introduce no additional choice beyond the fixed compactification.

proof.text: For the last assertion put $A=A_m$, $B=A_n$, and first work on the etale site. The dualizing objects $\omega_A^{\mathrm{et}}$ and $\omega_B^{\mathrm{et}}$ are bounded constructible of finite Tor amplitude by [lem-coef-dualizing-construction]. Their pro-etale realizations are the $\omega_m,\omega_n$ in the question by [lem-weil-finite-duality-site-comparison]. Since $X$ is separated of finite type over $k$, hence quasi-compact and quasi-separated, and $A_m$ is a finite, hence Noetherian, ring, [det-pe-finite-tor-comparison-noetherian] shows that $\omega_m\cong\nu_X^*\omega_A^{\mathrm{et}}$ is bounded constructible on $X_{\mathrm{proet}}$ with the same finite Tor amplitude $[a,b]$, as the next lemma requires. Apply [lem-fix-reduction-open-etale-origin] to $K=\omega_m$ and the fixed $j$. It gives bounded etale-origin witnesses for both $j_!\omega_m$ and its derived coefficient extension. Thus the bounded-below hypotheses of the etale/pro-etale proper scalar-mate comparison hold at the object to which $Rp_*$ is applied; no such hypothesis was needed in steps 1--6.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-etale-proetale-scalar-mate] to $p$ and the witnesses from step 7. It identifies the actual B-linear proper coefficient mate $b_p$ with the etale proper coefficient mate under the canonical tensor and direct-image comparisons. Its qcqs hypothesis holds since $p$ is proper. The open factor is equally the canonical one: [lem-fix-open-scalar-tensor-normalization] characterizes $\beta_j^{-1}$ as the open adjunct of the scalar/pullback comparison followed by the open unit. [lem-fix-site-open-exchange] characterizes the site/open comparison by that same unit normalization. The scalar/pullback cube of [lem-sfb-etale-proetale-scalar-pullback-cube] commutes, so pasting their open adjunction transposes with [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting] identifies the two open coefficient maps. Pasting this equality with the proper equality identifies $Rp_{*,n}(\beta_j)b_p$ with the finite pro-etale realization of the etale compact-support tensor comparison. By [lem-fix-compact-support-coefficient-change] this is precisely its canonical comparison at $\omega_A^{\mathrm{et}}$, the map denoted $c_{X,A,B,\omega_A}$ in [lem-coef-finite-dualizing]. All comparisons here concern the finite constructible realizations, not an exceptional adjoint on arbitrary pro-etale objects.

proof.text:
Under $M_m\cong\omega_m$ and $M_n\cong\omega_n$, the assumed $\alpha_{m,n}$ is the counit-defined $u_{m,n}$ of [lem-coef-finite-dualizing]. Substitute it into the already proved expression for $d_{m,n}$ in step 3, using the comparison identification of step 8. This gives exactly
$$d_{m,n}=\operatorname{Res}_{m,n}(F_n(u_{m,n})c_{m,n,\omega_m})\eta_{F_m\omega_m}.$$
The isomorphisms identifying the levels merely conjugate the same natural maps. This proves the conditional dualizing clause without changing the arbitrary-input assertion.
